subject: Private deployment: evidence stewarding, operator delegation & MSA/OF redlines
messages:

Cc: procurement@ozwellhealth.com
Date: 2026-10-12T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + OF redlines: operator stewardship & evidence access ask

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and infra teams reviewed the MSA/Order Form and returned redlines focused on private deployment controls. Two primary asks: operator delegation (who will operate the runtime in our environment) and an "evidence stewardship" path for auditability (snapshots, logs, and a witnessable transfer mechanism). I've attached our initial redlines (Initial_Redlines_Ozwell.pdf).

Specific asks we want to clarify before we share with procurement:
- A canonical list of artifacts you can provide for a private/VPC/on-prem deploy (snapshots, configured runbooks, operator account manifests, forensic logs).
- Whether Redwood will accept an escrow-style sealed snapshot deposit or support remote witness plus transfer.
- Language we can include in the OF to limit operator privileges and preserve auditability.

Can you send a short note with options (legal-friendly phrasing) and an evidence inventory we can use for our audit team? Our timeline is tight — ideally a response in 2 business days. Procurement is cc'd; they will want the technical option we plan to sign to.

Appreciate it — Claire
Ozwell Health — Sr. Counsel
[attachment: Initial_Redlines_Ozwell.pdf]

Claire — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines.

On Mon, Oct 12, 2026 at 9:22 AM Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@ozwellhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and infra teams reviewed the MSA/Order Form and returned redlines focused on private deployment controls.

We can take three pragmatic paths that map to the asks in your PDF. I'll keep the language high level here and attach a short evidence inventory and our redline to the MSA for legal.

Option A — Witnessed snapshot + handover (recommended):
- Redwood produces a time-stamped sealed snapshot of the deployment image + operator runbook and deposits it into a mutually agreed third-party escrow (simple MD5/sha256 manifests).
- Redwood provides a remote witnessing session where Ozwell's infra lead observes snapshot generation and transfer.
- Operational access remains with Ozwell; Redwood will provide operator runbook, sample operator accounts (read-only audit accounts), and a limited support account for emergency debugging.

Option B — Escrowed sealed deposit with notarized transfer:
- Redwood deposits encrypted snapshot + runbook into escrow accessible under defined triggers (termination, audit). Redwood retains a sealed copy with limited access controls.

Option C — Operator-stewardship (short-term managed operator):
- Redwood operates the runtime on Ozwell's dedicated infra under strict SLA and role-based access, with a documented rollback/runbook and monthly attestations.

Attached: RDW_MSA_v3_redline.pdf (we inserted MSA language proposals) and evidence_inventory.xlsx (canonical artifact list you requested).

Suggested next steps:
1) Legal picks preferred option (A/B/C).
2) If A or B: we provide clause wording and a short exhibit describing escrow triggers and witness process.
3) Schedule a 30-min infra call to walk through the witness demo (I can loop our infra lead).

We can turn around a draft exhibit and clause text within 48 hours once you pick a path.

Short note for procurement: the three options have different cost profiles — Option A is the most straightforward from a procurement perspective; Option C can carry a managed-services fee. Happy to map cost implications after you pick.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
[attachments: RDW_MSA_v3_redline.pdf, evidence_inventory.xlsx]

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: MSA + OF redlines: operator stewardship & evidence access ask — legal guidance

Sofia / Jordan — quick legal take and suggested clause text. I'm keeping this tight so we can move with Claire's 48-hour window.

On the operator delegation topic, we want to avoid permanent transfer of production code or keys. Suggested high-level principles to include in the OF:
- Limited license: Redwood grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to deploy the specified model runtime within the customer's designated infrastructure, solely for the customer's internal use; no right to copy or redistribute runtime artifacts outside escrow triggers.
- Escrow trigger: A sealed snapshot deposited with a neutral escrow agent becomes accessible to the customer if Redwood is (a) materially in breach and fails to cure within 30 days, or (b) permanently ceases business operations. Access requires dual authentication and notarized retrieval.
- Operator privileges: If Redwood performs short-term managed operations, we propose scoped operator accounts with an auditable action log, time-limited access tokens, and a monthly signed attestation of operations performed.

Clause sample (for redline):
"Escrowed Snapshot and Access. Upon execution of this Order Form, Redwood shall deposit an encrypted, time-stamped snapshot of the deployed runtime and associated operational documentation with the mutually agreed escrow agent. Customer shall only be entitled to retrieve and decrypt the snapshot upon the occurrence of an Escrow Release Event (as defined herein). Retrieval shall be subject to the escrow agent's standard retrieval procedures and require written confirmation from both parties; decryption keys shall be held in split-control."

We should avoid hard operational SLAs that require operator credentials to be handed over during normal operation — stick to escrow + witness + attestation language.

I'll attach legal_suggested_clauses.docx with a tidy redline. Recommend proposing Option A publicly and keeping B as a fallback; Option C we can price but escalate to PM/finance if they push for long-term managed ops.

-D
[attachment: legal_suggested_clauses.docx]
